hypothesis: The captured ROM's reset prefix and helper write the progress word at 0x07090304 as decoded, in both initial selector states and from forced-FEL entry.
conclusion: The decoded reset-path writes hold on the captured ROM image; the check does not establish later ROM-side writes or reset retention.
narrative: checks/watchdog-rom-reset-log.py (removed: a one-off ROM reset-log inspection, run as python checks/watchdog-rom-reset-log.py physical-rom.bin) executed the reset prefix and the ROM helper at 0xd14. Five cases passed: both initial selector states, direct forced-FEL entry, and both active halves in the helper. No instructions were skipped. The check stopped before FEL initialization, used synthetic MMIO and did not model reset retention. The capture also contains transfers to addresses beyond its end, including 0x11000 and 0x17000, so the check does not establish every later ROM-side write. The check and source hashes are retained in the evidence directory. The existing expiry, ROM-dispatch and hardware configuration checks were not repeated. No device access or physical measurement occurred.
